items.synopsis: The nsd process crashes on SRX platforms during cluster reboot, failover, or policy addition causes traffic outage
items.description: On all Junos OS SRX series platforms configured with the logical systems (LSYS), the network security daemon (nsd) process crashes due to cluster failover or reboot of node in a standalone firewall setup or while adding security policies. This crash generates a core dump and prevents the system from configuring security policies. As a result, all policy configurations are removed, leading to a traffic outage.

items.synopsis: Virtual Port Peer on vmhost interface behavior with 24.2R1
items.description: On the NFX platforms, the user can map front panel L2 interfaces to a single L3 interface by using the "peer-interface" command which is not as per the design which states that the mapping requires the knob "fail-on-any-peer".

items.synopsis: Packet drops can occur when packets are received with a size equal to the default MRU
items.description: On SRX1600, SRX2300 and SRX4300 platforms, when packets are received with a size matching the default MRU (Maximum Receive Unit) value of 1522 bytes, packets are dropped, leading to an impact on traffic.

items.synopsis: CoS shaping is not functional on IRB interfaces when the SRX1600 is in switching mode
items.description: On SRX1600 platform, Class of Service (CoS) shaping does not work on IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) interfaces.

items.synopsis: L3VPN routes are not advertised to peer when BGP sessions with route-target filter flaps
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, after Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) sessions configured with 'family route-target' flaps, delayed route deletion causes the loss of the Route Target Filter (RTF), preventing the node from advertising L3VPN (Layer 3 Virtual Private Network) and direct routes (e.g., loopbacks and interface routes) to the BGP peer, leading to VPN route loss and service disruption.

items.synopsis: Incorrect subcode NOTIFICATION is sent when local interface is disabled for which multihop is configured for directly connected peer
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when 'multihop' is configured on a directly connected interface towards a peer and the session goes in IDLE state due to no local interface (interface is disabled or down), the log messages shows 'subcode 6 'Other Configuration Change'' instead of 'subcode 9 'Hard Reset''.

items.synopsis: BGP route advertisement failure with as-override and peer-as configured at group level
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, BGP ( Border Gateway Protocol ) fails to advertise routes to external peers in an L3VPN ( Layer 3 Virtual Private Network ) environment when as-override is configured for a neighbor on the local device, and peer-as is applied at the group level. Since the routes are not advertised to peers, traffic matching those routes are dropped, causing service disruption.

items.synopsis: Slow commits and chassisd cores on backup RE
items.description: On Junos VMHOST platforms, the delay in SSH session execution results in a delay in configuration commits and commit checks, which in turn causes a chassisd core dump.

items.synopsis: The chassisd process crash is seen after the device reboot when chassisd stalls after configuration commit
items.description: On all VMHost platforms, the chassisd crash can be seen, which can also lead to mastership switchover. This is mainly caused by a configuration commit (no specific configuration required) followed by a reboot.

items.synopsis: EX3400 Dot1x Radius accounting send incorrect value to the server for Acct-Input-Gigawords/ Acct-Output-Gigawords
items.description: With Dot1x Radius Authentication and Accounting, when the Stop Accounting (due to disconnect) is sent to the Radius server the Acct-Input-Gigawords and the Acct-Output-Gigawords contains unexpectedly large value.

items.synopsis: The l2ald process crash is observed on non L2NG Junos platforms configured with "native-vlan-id" and "bridge-domains" on an IFL
items.description: On non L2NG (Layer2 Next Generation) Junos EX, MX and SRX platforms, the l2ald (Layer 2 Address Learning Daemon) process crash is observed when an IFL (Logical Interface) configured with "native-vlan-id" and "bridge-domains" and when certain config change takes place in an IFL which maps VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) index to NULL. The dereferencing of this NULL pointer causes the crash.

items.synopsis: On ACX7348/ACX7332 all traffic is blocked on FPC after RE Switchover
items.description: On ACX7348/ACX7332 with MACsec enabled in channelized interfaces, after performing a double RE switchover (primary RE swap to backup and then back to active), traffic in FPC1 stops in being forwarded.

items.synopsis: Radius authentication is failing when Challenge Token is entered
items.description: On all Junos and Evo platforms, the Radius Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) failing for user login if the password and token were provided in two separate steps.

items.synopsis: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, HTTPS download fails when HTTPS URL is present in the configuration
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, when HTTPS URL is present as a part of file or mentioned explicitly in the configuration, and when there is a download attempted through this file the download fails. However, this is will not impact the forwarding traffic only the download through HTTPS will fail.

items.synopsis: 'TLV type 00000052 not supported on IFL gr' seen repeatedly in syslog for EVPN routing-instance configured with gr- ifls
items.description: JUNOS/EVO platforms running 23.4R2 and later software, if they have EVPN routing-instances with gr- ifls as members, continuous 'TLV not supported' messages could be seen in syslog.

items.synopsis: Stale MAC entries may remain in the MAC table of EVPN routing instances after rapid MAC-IP move scenarios
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms with EVPN-MPLS (Ethernet Virtual Private Network - Multiprotocol Label Switching) setup , stale MAC entries may remain in the MAC table of the EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) routing instances during rapid MAC-IP move scenarios. This can cause MAC tables to reach their limits preventing new MAC addresses learning and user registration.

items.synopsis: EX3400: "Error:tvp_optics_eeprom_read: Failed to read eeprom for link" syslog error message
items.description: "Error:tvp_optics_eeprom_read: Failed to read eeprom for link" logs might be seen for some time during system reboot or pfe restart in EX3400. There is no functional impact due to these logs.

items.synopsis: Packet drops when jumbo frames forwarded through ge interfaces configured for 10/100Mbps speed
items.description: On EX4300-MP platforms, ge (Gigabit ethernet) interfaces configured for 10 or 100Mbps (Mega bits per second), jumbo frame packets will be dropped.

items.synopsis: Interface goes down after a dc-pfe (Data Centre Packet Forwarding Engine) process restart in a Virtual Chassis environment on EX4400 platform
items.description: On a EX4400 virtual chassis environment, if the dc-pfe process restart for any reasons or restarted manually, then there is a possibility of some interfaces going down.

items.synopsis: TDR test can cause a CPU hog and result in BFD flaps
items.description: On the EX4100-F-12P, EX4100-F-12T, EX4100-24MP, EX4400-24MP, and EX4400-48MP platforms, running a TDR (Time-Domain Reflectometry) test specifically on mge interface, can cause a CPU (Central Processing Unit) hog and result in BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) flaps.

items.synopsis: For Junos OS platforms, the OSPF neighborship gets stuck in EXSTART state after performing NSSU
items.description: For Junos OS platforms, in a specific configuration change after NSSU (Nonstop Software Upgrade), i.e. delete and add sequence of LAG (Link Aggregation Group) bundles performed via load baseline configuration and re-apply original configuration, OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) session might get stuck in EXSTART state. This issue will impact the traffic.

items.synopsis: STP/MSTP/RSTP/VSTP convergence issue due to BPDU drop by l2cpd
items.description: On Junos EX4K and QFX5K platforms, STP (Spanning Tree Protocol)/MSTP (Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol) /RSTP (Rapid Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol) /VSTP (Vlan Spanning Tree Protocol) convergence issues were observed due to BPDUs (Bridge Protocol Data Units) being dropped by the l2cpd (Layer 2 Control Protocol Daemon) process. This behavior prevents STP/MSTP/RSTP/VSTP from converging successfully, impacting network stability.

items.synopsis: Default Route configured with Discard Next Hop on PFE instead of ECMP Next Hop after reboot
items.description: On all Junos EX4K (except EX4300) in a VC (Virtual Chassis) environment using LPM (Longest Prefix Match) routing, after a reboot the default route on the PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) is incorrectly set to a "discard next-hop (NH)" instead of an ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi-Path) next-hop resulting in connectivity issues.

items.synopsis: The SRX1500 drops the packet if MTU matches the MRU of the receiving device
items.description: On SRX1500 platforms, if the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) is configured to match the Maximum Receive Unit (MRU) of the receiving device, packet drops occur. This occurs because additional processing overhead increases the packet size beyond the MRU limit, causing the receiving device to drop the packets.

items.synopsis: JUNOS MX | iflset stats not getting cleared after issuing clear interfaces stats all and clear interfaces interface-set statistics all CLI command
items.description: JUNOS MX | iflset stats not getting cleared after issuing clear interfaces stats all and clear interfaces interface-set statistics all CLI command

items.category: Libjtask for RPD tasks, scheduler, timers, memory, and slip
items.synopsis: Memory Leak: Memory leak is detected with rpd task blocks "rpd-trace"
items.description: Memory Leak: Memory leak is detected with rpd task blocks "rpd-trace"

items.category: JFlow bug tracker for SRX platforms
items.synopsis: Application crash is observed due to insufficient memory when a large number of JFlow entries are created
items.description: On Junos OS SRX platforms with JFlow configured with sampling interval set to 1, traffic impact is observed due to insufficient memory for the Layer 7 applications leading to application failure. The issue happens when a large number of JFlow entries are created exhausting memory potentially leading to crash.

items.category: Adresses ALG issues found in JSF
items.synopsis: The SRX platform may experience a flowd process crash and generate core dump files when the ALG feature is enabled
items.description: On SRX platforms running the Junos Operating System (OS) with Application Layer Gateway (ALG) enabled, in rare scenarios, flowd process can crash and crash files are generated. While the platform eventually recovers, traffic loss will occur during this process.

items.synopsis: PIM IP ESP packet fragments dropped in SRX platform
items.description: Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) fragmented packets using IP Protocol 50 (Encapsulating Security Payload - ESP) are dropped when traversing SRX devices operating in flow mode.

items.synopsis: Security forwarding process crash may occur when multicast traffic triggers a route resolution request that needs to be processed for a pending session
items.description: When multicast traffic triggers a route resolution request for a pending session, and the route is subsequently resolved, a race condition may occur if that pending session is terminated by a different thread before processing can continue. This can result in a crash of the flowd (security forwarding process). However, the control plane remains online and unaffected.

items.synopsis: PFE crash is observed when PFE processes the traffic passing through the dedicated fabric link
items.description: On the Junos OS SRX4600 platform, when PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) processes the IPv4/IPv6 traffic passes through the dedicated fabric link, PFE crash is observed. This issue happens when PMI (PowerMode IPsec) is enabled (by default) and flow session accessing stale values.

items.synopsis: L3MNHA with SRG1 IPSEC : MNHA ICL ipsec encryption link went down permanently after rebooting connected router through which ICL was established before. During this state IKE process got stuck at ~70% on MNHA Active node.
items.description: Generic MNHA issue not specific to CSDS

items.category: all logging related bugs on srx platforms
items.synopsis: Security log report messages w.r.t logical system is not generated
items.description: show security log report cli command for logical systems is not working for 24.2R2, 24.4R1-S2, if log report is disabled under root system. Work around is available for this issue.

items.synopsis: The "show security match-policies" command results in a timeout error
items.description: On all SRX platforms, when a scaled DNS (Domain Name System) configuration with approximately 500 entries is applied along with a policy configuration, issuing the "show security match-policies" command results in a timeout error. This issue has no functional impact.

items.synopsis: Failed inter-process communication results in higher heap and buffer usage which impacts the functionality of processes
items.description: On all Junos SRX platforms, when there is a broken Inter-Process Communication (IPC) link between the Routing Engine (RE) and Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE), heap and buffer utilization gradually increase to 99%, causing some software modules to start failing.

items.synopsis: Wrong service-name display in SRX RT_FLOW traffic log.
items.description: On SRX platforms, wrong service-name might display in SRX RT_FLOW traffic log.

items.synopsis: NSD file handles incrementing consistently in database file causing a rare condition of ssh access failure
items.description: On all Junos SRX branch platforms, Network Security Daemon(NSD) file handles increments consistently. Triggering a rare condition of ssh access failure of the device.

items.synopsis: SRX PFE crash is observed with source-identity enabled
items.description: On all SRX platforms with source-identify and logging enabled, the PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) crashes if the source identity username and group-names exceeds certain count and length. The system self-recovers after the issue is hit.

items.synopsis: Type 5 EVPN traffic is dropped on SRX when PMI is disabled or not supported
items.description: On all SRX platforms, in an EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN) environment, when PMI (Power Mode IPSec) is disabled or not supported, type 5 EVPN traffic gets dropped. The issue occurs due to flow context being cleared incorrectly, causing the overlay JEXEC nexthop to be pushed after the underlay one. This leads to the packet being treated as multicast and subsequently dropped.

items.synopsis: L2ald process crash is observed upon executing hidden command "show ethernet-switching debug-statistics fast-mac-update" in case the command doesn't have any output
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, the l2ald process crash is observed upon executing the hidden command "show ethernet-switching debug-statistics fast-mac-update" in case the command doesn't have any output.

items.category: Issues related to Junos licensing infrastructure
items.synopsis: Subscribers unable to connect in GNF setup
items.description: On Junos MX platforms with Node Slicing, i.e., GNF (Guest Network Function), and Subscriber Management services enabled, Subscriber bring-up failure can occur when an upgrade is performed from a non-Agile License infra release to a release running Agile-based Licensing. This issue impacts subscriber services and is encountered due to the enforced Hard Licensing feature for node slicing.

items.category: Issues related to Junos licensing infrastructure
items.synopsis: [MX] "smid ../../../../../../src/junos/lib/libsdb/licsubs/bsd12/liblicense_subs_os.c liblic_subs_total_active_licenses_in_use XXX" logs flood in license_flex_subs_trace.log.
items.description: "smid ../../../../../../src/junos/lib/libsdb/licsubs/bsd12/liblicense_subs_os.c liblic_subs_total_active_licenses_in_use XXX" messages can be seen so frequent interval in license_flex_subs_trace.log.

items.synopsis: On MX10K4, MX10K8, MX10K16 systems, in some cases, a SPMB PFE (spmbpfe)core might be seen when system is going down.
items.description: On MX10K4, MX10K8, MX10K16 systems , a SPMB PFE (spmbpfe) may occationally create a core file when the system is being shutdown. This event adds 10 seconds to the time to shut the system down. The delay dues to the PTP FPGA reset sequence during the shutdown process.

items.synopsis: Link instability is seen on 4x10GSR and 40G-SR4 SFP modules from Finisar having high Rx output value
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC10E line cards, having SFPs from Finisar like 4x10GSR and 40G-SR4 plugged into the chassis results in high Rx (Receive) output values, causing link instability.

items.synopsis: The rpd crash due to memory corruption in PIM/MSDP network
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, enabling PIM (Protocol Independent Multicast) or MSDP (Multicast Source Discovery Protocol) may cause a rare memory corruption during the update of the MSDP Source Active route. This issue primarily affects highly scaled environments, leading to rpd (routing protocol daemon) coredumps and potential traffic loss.

items.synopsis: The self-generated traffic on Junos platforms use the incorrect source IP with ECMP configuration
items.description: On all Junos platforms configured with Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) routing, self-generated traffic selects an incorrect source (Internet Protocol) IP address. As a result, the peer device lacks the relevant route information, causing self-generated traffic to be dropped. This issue is specific to ECMP configurations and does not impact data traffic.

items.synopsis: FTP default mode changed from active to passive on 24.2R2
items.description: An upgrade to libfetch caused the default FTP mode to move from active to passive. This PR corrects this as customers more than likely expect the previous active FTP functionality on their networks.

items.synopsis: Image validation fails during the Junos VM validation.
items.description: On all Junos platforms that use pkgs/junos-vmguest/mtx/vmhost-pkg-support when loading image to 25.3+, image validation fails.

items.synopsis: Complete packet loss will be observed for the inter-VLAN traffic in EVPN-VXLAN CRB scenario
items.description: On Junos QFX and EX platforms in an EVPN-VXLAN (Extended Virtual Private Network- Virtual Extensible LAN) CRB (Centrally-Routed Bridging) scenario where the ingress leaf switch is configured with ESI (Ethernet Segment Identifier) lags (i.e. the server is multihomed), if there is an overlap between ESI lag(s) trunk ID with physical port number(s) and overlap of DMAC (destination MAC) between VGA (Virtual Gateway Address) MAC address 00:00:5e:00:01:01 (CRB setup with VGA / GW is on spine) with VRRP (Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol) MAC (specifically for the VRRP group 1 MAC address 00:00:5e:00:01:01) on the physical ports of the Leaf switches, then traffic loss will be observed for the inter-VLAN traffic.

items.synopsis: Protocol traffic drops were seen in the network for any configuration change in the protocol
items.description: On all Junos QFX5K platforms, with ECMP (Equal Cost Multi Path) configured, when there is any routing protocol change (like ISIS cost metric change), the protocol traffic on the network is dropped.

items.synopsis: Traffic drop observed due to ECMP next-hop programming issue
items.description: On QFX5k, EX4k, EX2300 and EX3400 platforms, ECMP next-hop programming issue causes some prefixes to drop traffic. The issue is observed when the software-configured ECMP size (maximum-ecmp) exceeds the limit of 64 during a network churn event in the network. This triggers ECMP to skip updates, leading to stale forwarding paths and a temporary traffic freeze.

items.synopsis: The dcpfe process crashes on all Junos QFX and EX platforms due to memory corruption
items.description: A memory corruption issue can result random dcpfe (dense concentrator packet forwarding engine) process crashes on all Junos QFX and EX platforms configured with VXLAN (Virtual Extensible Local Area Network) configuration.

items.synopsis: Command "show pfe vxlan" is not supported on QFX5200 devices
items.description: Support added for "show pfe vxlan" CLI command on QFX 5200 devices

items.synopsis: Memory Corruption in Function for MULTICAST Components
items.description: On all QFX5k Junos Operation Systems, memory corruption is detected during the execution of function which triggers a call to the abort function via the panic function with the message "Memory corruption in block" leading to application crash causing service impact.

items.category: QFX5K JUNOS Interface, MACSec, Optics, SDK, PHY
items.synopsis: Interface flap between the QFX5120 and QFX5210 with QSFP-100G-LR4-T2 optics
items.description: When the 100G port with QSFP-100G-LR4-T2 is used the interface is negotiating to CAUI4 and when this happens the Speed needs to be explicitly set which was missing in the code.

items.synopsis: Auto-negotiation issue will be observed on 10ge-type SFP in QFX5120-48YM platform
items.description: On Junos QFX5120-48YM platforms, auto-negotiation is not enabled for 10ge-type transceivers. Resulting in the port remaining down when connected to a peer device with 1G/10G.

items.synopsis: Unintended reboots on QFX5120-48Y and EX4650-48Y platforms with Acbel PSU
items.description: On QFX5120-48Y and EX4650-48Y platforms with Acbel PSU (Power Supply Unit) sudden reboots are seen during UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) switchover. This results in impact on the traffic switchover.

items.synopsis: Memory leak is detected when interfaces are configured
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, 72-byte size memory leak is seen when interface configuration is added. But there is no traffic impact due to this issue.

items.category: Remote Access VPN issues on SRX
items.synopsis: Hostname with apostrophe causing connection failures on SRX
items.description: On all SRX platforms, a character restriction prevents Remote Access VPN connections when the hostname includes an apostrophe. Any device with a hostname containing an apostrophe will fail to connect to SRX using Juniper Secure Connect. This issue is not limited to mobile devices and can affect any device using Remote Access VPN with a hostname that meets the affecting criteria.

items.synopsis: The commit command failed due to a speed mismatch between the Ten-Gigabit Ethernet (XE) port and the Aggregated Ethernet (AE) interface to which it belongs
items.description: On all platforms running the Junos Operating System (OS), the commit command fails when the speed of XE interfaces is downgraded using a Small Form-factor Pluggable (SFP) module, causing a speed mismatch with the AE interface to which they belong. However, this does not affect the overall operation of the AE interface.

items.synopsis: Flexible-vlan-tagging option is missing under interface hierarchy on SRX3xx series
items.description: On SRX3xx series configured with flexible-vlan-tagging, after upgrading the device to Junos version 23.4R2 or higher the flexible-vlan-tagging option is missing under the interface hierarchy. This leads to a syntax error, stopping users from setting the flexible-vlan-tagging.

items.category: ZT/YTpfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: In an EVPN with IRB solution underlying NH change can cause packet drops on certain MX/EX platforms
items.description: On Junos MX with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 line cards and EX92K platforms, , when IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) is configured under EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) routing instance, and any event that cause changes in the existing target of indirect NH (Next Hop) to a new target, the new target's token is not updated in IRB NH, will result in OOO (Out of Order) errors and packet drops.

items.synopsis: The aftd process crash is seen on Junos OS platforms running MPC10, MPC11, LC4800, LC9600 line cards and in Junos OS platforms MX304, EX9200-15C
items.description: On Junos OS platforms running MPC10, MPC11, LC4800, LC9600 line cards and in Junos OS platforms MX304, EX9200-15C, aftd process crash is seen resulting in crash of FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) line card while the route module of PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) processing route churns as simultaneous actions (add/delete/read) by multiple threads on the process.

items.synopsis: FPC crash will be seen due to memory access violation
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 and MX304, the FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) will crash, generating a coredump due to memory access violation. This will result in traffic loss until the FPC recovers on its own.

items.synopsis: ICMPv6 packets may be dropped instead of being translated using MAP-T
items.description: Depending on the configuration in use, on Junos MX platforms with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 line cards and all Junos Evolved platforms, ICMPv6 packets may be dropped instead of being translated using MAP-T.

items.category: Trio pfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: Octet and frame count is displayed incorrectly in jnxMacStatsEntry.
items.description: On all MX platforms with MPC10, MPC11 and LC9600, when the SNMP query is run using the command "show snmp mib walk jnxMac" . The output of jnxMacStatsEntry provides statistics from one of logical unit only even if there are multiple logical units configured and the vlan id information shows up as "0", whatever the actual vlan id is. This is a display issue with no impact.

items.category: Trio pfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: ARP packet drops seen if proxy-arp restricted is configured on an IRB interface.
items.description: On the Junos MX and EX9K platforms, when a Bridge Domain(BD) is configured with an integrated Routing and Bridging(IRB) interface that has proxy ARP set to restricted mode, the switch forwards ARP requests only to the Routing Engine(RE) without broadcasting them across the VLAN. Thus, impacting the hosts within the same VLAN.

items.synopsis: IPv6 neighbor discovery with DHCP packet getting dropped when no-snoop option is enabled for DHCP Relay
items.description: On Junos OS MX platforms with DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) Relay configured using the "no-snoop" option, DHCP packets are not being processed correctly. This prevents next-hop resolution for the DHCP packets, causing IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) Neighbor Discovery with DHCP packet to be dropped by an intermediate device. As a result, the client fails to obtain an IP address, leading to traffic impact.

items.synopsis: Observing out-of-order packets when the TCP traffic gets passed over AE bundle and tunnelled via MPLSoUDP tunnel
items.description: On Junos OS platforms, When "dynamic tunnels" configured and "set chassis loopback-dynamic-tunnel" knob is used and when TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) traffic passed via MPLSoUDP (Multi-Protocol Label Switching Over User Datagram Protocol) tunnel through an outgoing AE (Aggregated Ethernet) bundle interface having member interfaces, use of either inner or outer header hash calculations lead to out-of-order packets at the egress. It causes service impact on related flow of traffic due to out-of-order packets.

items.synopsis: On SRX300 series DHCP relay stops working and the device generates coredump after upgrading to JunOS 23.4R2-S2.1
items.description: On SRX300 series devices, when TACACS accounting is configured, after an upgrade to Junos 23.4R2-S2.1, the DHCP-relay may not work anymore and the shm-rtsdbd process may produce coredumps.

items.synopsis: User root is shown as incorrect after power cycle of the device
items.description: After a power cycle, telnet login through the console fails. The issue occurs randomly and does not happen after every power cycle. To recover the device, another power cycle should be performed.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: cli coredump genarated when the size of buffer area (user input) increased to 1GB
items.description: Cli coredump genarated when the size of buffer area (user input) increased to 1GB.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: Unexpected issues such as login failures or disabled interfaces observed following abrupt reboot during commit operation
items.description: On Junos platforms with boot-time optimization enabled, an abrupt reboot during a commit operation can cause configuration file corruption, potentially leading to issues like login failures or disabled interfaces.

items.synopsis: FPC crashing when web filtering type set to "juniper-enhanced" or "NG-juniper"
items.description: On all SRX platforms, when the web-filtering type set to "juniper-enhanced" or "NG-juniper" (NextGen-juniper), it might cause FPC (Flexible Port Concentrator) card crash and with "srxpfe" or "lcore" crash files generated.

items.synopsis: LLDP is failing to operate on the vSRX series platform
items.description: On vSRXv3 Platforms using Mellanox ConnectX-5 (MLX5) Virtual Function (VF) as Network Interface Card (NIC), even when the Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) is enabled, it does not function at all, resulting in packets with LLDP multicast destination MAC addresses being dropped by the MLX5 NIC.

items.synopsis: Split brain scenario is observed on vSRX3.0 with public cloud MNHA deployment
items.description: On vSRX3.0 platforms with public cloud (Azure/AWS/GCP) MNHA (Multinode High Availability) setup when manually failed over, split brain scenario will be observed.

items.synopsis: The srxpfe process crash is observed on vSRX platform after set disable on the ge- interface and then rollback
items.description: The srxpfe process crashes when disabling the ge- interface mapped to an SR-IOV interface, followed by a rollback. This issue cause a traffic impact.

items.synopsis: Traffic drops on ge interfaces configured for PTP
items.description: On ACX2200 series, ge (gigabit ethernet) interfaces configured for PTP (Precision Time Protocol), after PTP is deactivated and activated or activated for the first time, traffic can experience packet drops.

items.synopsis: The L2BSA subscriber fails to logout when "auto-configure-trigger" knob is edited on ANCP neighbour of MX platforms
items.description: On all MX platforms with Access Node Control Protocol(ANCP) configured, the knob auto-configure-trigger on ANCP neighbor if edited (deactivate and activate) between system boot-ups, is not getting applied to the ANCP neighbour correctly. As a result, if an ANCP session goes down and the adjacency-loss-hold-time expires, the Layer 2 Bit Stream Access(L2BSA) interface still remains up indefinitely and the subscribers will fail to logout. Chassis needs to be rebooted after editing the configuration.

items.synopsis: Updating a source-file to load ROAs should be done by changing the name of the source file
items.description: Loading ROAs from a source-file was a feature introduced as a convenience feature and as such this only affects that feature. This feature is not in widespread use and was created to have a fallback ROA when all sessions go down. This problem scenario requires multiple reloads with the being modified back and forth to add and then delete and re-add the database configured in the import policy.

items.synopsis: BGP queue deadlock on Junos/Junos OS Evolved/cRPD platforms leading to route advertisement failure and traffic loss
items.description: On all Junos, Junos OS Evolved, and cRPD platforms, due to deadlock in internal processes, BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) route advertisement fails leading to traffic disruption.

items.synopsis: BGP updates missing graceful-shutdown community after quick sender knob flaps
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when the graceful-shutdown sender knob is repeatedly deleted and subsequently re-added in quick intervals under a BGP-LU (Border Gateway Protocol-Labeled Unicast) session, the router CLI (command line interface) incorrectly indicates that the graceful-shutdown community is being advertised. However, the actual BGP update messages sent over the session do not include the graceful-shutdown community. This results in the graceful-shutdown community not being propagated to BGP peers during graceful shutdown events, which will potentially cause traffic forwarding issues.

items.synopsis: rpd crash when changes are applied to as-path with dynamic-db in use
items.description: On Junos OS platforms using as-path-groups (Autonomous System Path Group) with dynamic-db (dynamic Data base) feature enabled, rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) may crash after as-path configuration changes.

items.synopsis: Observing traffic loss on PS service interface after deactivate and activate VPLS/EVPN instance type
items.description: On all Junos platforms with PS (Pseudowire Subscriber Interfaces), when PS interface is configured with multiple logical units and the transport interface (PS unit 0) is configured interface family type as VPLS or bridge and when deleting routing instance corresponds to transport interface causing the associated service interfaces packets to be dropped and traffic impact will be seen for the associated service interfaces.

items.category: EVO Netstack Juniper Tunnel Driver Module
items.synopsis: Memory leak is observed when Telemetry is configured
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms having Telemetry configured, the memory allocations in 512 bytes slab that are seen to be growing in problem state, are related to write on a unix domain socket (internal to application). Since the data is not read, the send buffer keeps growing and the associated memory does not gets released. Every telemetry response from the producer does a 1 byte write on this socket and over a period of time the send buffer gets full. The default size of the unix socket send buffer is set to 512MB. But there is no functional impact.

items.synopsis: Deactivating protocol evpn in a routing-instance configured with 'vrf-target auto' leads to the rpd crash on both REs
items.description: On all MX platforms the deactivation a routing-instance configured with 'vrf-target auto' while also configured with protocol evpn (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) leads to the rpd crash in all the REs (Routing Engine) present in the chassis

items.synopsis: On EX2300, EX3400, :EX4300-48MP and EX4300 , Pause frames counters does not get incremented when pause frames are sent.
items.description: On EX2300, EX3400, :EX4300-48MP and EX4300 , Pause frames counters does not get incremented when pause frames are sent.

items.synopsis: Random ports of EX4400 will not be created on upgrade or reboot
items.description: On EX4400, any fiber SFP plugged into EX4400-24X PIC 0 ports or EX4400-48F PIC 0 ports 36-47, random interfaces will not be created when the device is upgraded or rebooted. Interfaces will not be listed in the device and will affect all functionalities of the optic or interface.

items.synopsis: EX2300/EX3400 : The status LED of uplink port is not working properly
items.description: On EX2300 and EX3400, the status LED of uplink port always displays green regardless of the status of the link.

items.synopsis: EX4100: 10g-BASE-T didn't come up after dc-pfe restart
items.description: After multiple iterations of dc-pfe process restart, we may see interface with 10g-base-t transceiver (part# 740-123734) will not come up.

items.synopsis: The SRX1500 drops the packet if MTU matches the MRU of the receiving device
items.description: On SRX1500 platforms, if the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) is configured to match the Maximum Receive Unit (MRU) of the receiving device, packet drops occur. This occurs because additional processing overhead increases the packet size beyond the MRU limit, causing the receiving device to drop the packets.

items.synopsis: JDI-RCT-MPC10E: Ksyncd crash on backup RE after fpc reboot
items.description: On MX series, when PS over RLT is configured where all member LTs are hosted on the same FPC and user restarts this FPC then on rare occasion, ksyncd crash can occur on backup RE. However, there is no impact on the master and only backup RE is affected. This issue is not consistent and seen only once out of ~10 or 15 fpc restart operations.

items.synopsis: Type 5 VXLAN traffic drops are observed when SRX run as L3-VNI gateway and the ingress and egress traffic goes to the same Type-5 VXLAN peer
items.description: On Junos OS SRX platforms running as L3-VNI (Layer 3 - Virtual Network Identifier) gateway in EVPN-VxLAN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network - Virtual Extensible LAN) scenario, traffic drops will be observed if traffic passes through two VxLAN tunnels and traffic fails to cross the two VxLAN tunnels when the PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) is processing the packet having same remote IPs for two VXLAN tunnels.

items.synopsis: IPSec tunnel inactive after multiple srg failovers on SRX platforms
items.description: On all SRX platforms, IPSec tunnels remain inactive if multiple Service Redundancy Group (SRG) failovers occur within a short period. This issue is specifically observed when the IPSec VPN is configured with the default establish on traffic setting. During rapid failovers, if high volumes of traffic are present, the tunnel re-establishment process fails, leading to inactive tunnels and potential traffic disruption.

items.synopsis: MX104 AFEB might crash following a change of PTP clock source.
items.description: On MX104, the AFEB could crash and reboot following a change of PTP GM clock source, which affects traffic forwarding.

items.synopsis: The SPC3 card resets due to kernel memory exhaustion in MX Series platforms with highly scaled routing tables and Inline Active Flow Monitoring configured
items.description: On MX240, MX480 and MX960 platforms with MX-SPC3 (Services Processing Card) service cards, when Inline Active Flow Monitoring (inline-jflow) is configured in a highly scaled routing environment (~4M routes), the SPC3 service card runs out of kernel memory, resulting in the PIC going offline or resetting and the services running on the SPC3 card gets disrupted.

items.synopsis: ON QFX5K and EX4K platforms a log is required for route leaking when destination table hits a platform limitation
items.description: On Junos QFX5K and Junos EX4K switches, route leaking for IPv4 requires a minimum route mask of /16, and the leak destination table must have a prefix length longer than or equal to that of the leak prefix for proper routing. When this doesn't occur, traffic forwarding is affected, and there is no log associated with this event

items.category: RPD Next-hop issues including indirect, CNH, and MCNH
items.synopsis: Next-hop APIs to support LDP stitching cases over BGP routes pointing to list of indirects
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms this is an enhancement for Nexthop APIs to support LDP stitching cases over BGP routes pointing to list of indirects next-hops.

items.synopsis: Load balance hash-key forwarding persists when switching to Layer 3-only
items.description: On Junos SRX4600, SRX1600, SRX2300 and SRX4300 platforms, when switching load balance from L3+L4 to L3, hash-key forwarding fails; the device retains L3+L4.

items.category: Trio pfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: STP/RSTP/MSTP/VSTP enters a disputed and blocked state when the anchor FPC of an AE link, with members distributed across multiple FPCs, goes offline
items.description: On MX and EX9200 series platforms that operate in hyper mode by default, STP (Spanning Tree Protocol)/RSTP (Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol)/MSTP (Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol)/VSTP (VLAN Spanning Tree Protocol) transitions to a disputed and blocked state if the members of the AE (Aggregated Ethernet) link in the anchor FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) goes offline.

items.synopsis: Unable establish gnmi session using Radius and TACACS auth
items.description: Unable establish gnmi session using Radius and TACACS auth. Currently JADE (Junoscript authentication daemon) utility which does authentication for telemetry on cRPD has support for local authentication.

items.category: Configuration mgmt, ffp, load-action, commit processing
items.synopsis: Netconf RPC commit fails due to commit warning received for unprotect operation, CLI commit completes with warning
items.description: In Netconf private edit configuration session, commit RPC fails when unprotect operation is performed.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: CLI stops responding when Ctrl+Z is pressed
items.description: On Junos 24.2 or later releases using BSD15, cli process may be suspended when Ctrl+Z is pressed in CLI.

items.synopsis: JUNOS: Netconf: Edit-config with operation attribute create for existing hierarchy is not working as per RFC 6241
items.description: JUNOS: Netconf: Edit-config with operation attribute create for existing hierarchy is not working as per RFC 6241

items.category: Issues related to YANG Data Models
items.synopsis: Few yang package are occuring multiple place On Box
items.description: Few yang package are occuring multiple place On Box

items.synopsis: JUNOS_REG: MX10008 : Observing core-spmbpfe at cmty_doob_rcb_fpga_init, cmty_spmb_hw_init, cmty_spmb_module_init, __pthread_kill_implementation, __kernel_vsyscall
items.description: spmbpfe core can be seen sometimes in these two case: 1. During ISSU when old master RE comes up with the new image, a spmbpfe core is generated when the old master RE goes down after reboot is given post new image installation. The core will be seen post the reboot. 2. When "request system reboot" cli command is executed, a spmbpfe core will occur when the junos goes down and the core will be seen post the system comes up. These cores generated at these stages will have no impact on a running system. The core are seen only when some kind of reboot is triggered.
